Park max depth 45 ft (14m), 2.5 miles of trail confirmed by official site + Scuba Diving Magazine.

tags.name: SS Dauntless
tags.notes: RE-AUDITED 2026-08-26. CORRECTION: prior note claimed the Dauntless was "owned by the Moe Brothers and retired from service in 1923" -- this is wrong. Per Wikipedia (Dauntless (steamboat)): built 1899 by Matthew McDowell at Tacoma, 93 ft, 91 tons; sold by builder to the Moe Brothers in 1900 for Bainbridge Island service; the Moe Brothers sold her again in 1902 to L.B. Hastings and Capt. Mann of Port Townsend for the Port Townsend-Irondale run -- she was under Hastings/Mann ownership, not Moe Brothers, when she broke loose from moorings at Appletree Cove (Kingston) in a storm on Dec 30 1923 and washed up/broke apart at Meadow Point. Confirmed by 2 independent sources (Wikipedia + nwdiveclub.com dive reports, which also confirm the wreck is regularly dived from Shilshole's Eddie Vine ramp, ~35 min bottom time reported Jan 2009). Depth ~21m (70ft) per boat-access dive reports. No confirmed vessel tonnage/dimension conflicts found.

tags.description: Wreck of a PB4Y-2 Privateer (BuNo 59695) that crashed Aug 26 1956 in Lake Washington during takeoff from NAS Sand Point with flaps retracted. 11-man crew evacuated safely; two crew received minor injuries. Navy salvage raised the aircraft Aug 31 1956, but a shackle pin on the hoisting sling failed during the tow and it re-sank; further salvage was abandoned as uneconomical. DEPTH: sources give different figures for different phases -- pacificnorthwestdiving.com's dive account describes the approach/guide line starting around 30 ffw and reaching the wreck line near 90 ffw, while aviation-safety.net's accident record states the aircraft's documented resting depth is approximately 155 ft, and that it sank to 210 ft at one point when the salvage sling failed. Given this spread, and that the OSM node records 47m (~154 ft), we report the resting depth as approximately 150-155 ft (46-47m) with the caveat that diver accounts of reaching the wreck line describe shallower figures, likely reflecting the guideline/approach path rather than the aircraft's final depth. Technical/decompression dive; GUE Seattle has produced photogrammetry documentation.
tags.name: Wreck of a PB4Y bomber
tags.notes: DEPTH CONFLICT FLAGGED: Wreck line accessed at ~90 ft ffw per pacificnorthwestdiving.com; other sources cite 150 ft (45m).
